questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.learningObjective: Interpret the appeal for refuge and its stated dangers, including its relation to An-Nās.
questions.prompt: Explain how the general request in Al-Falaq 113:2 relates to the more specific dangers named in verses 3–5.
questions.answer: Verse 2 gives the appeal a broad scope. The later verses identify particular dangers within that appeal.
questions.explanation: The progression moves from a general request to named instances.

markingGuide.description: Recognises the general scope of verse 2.
Explains the later verses as specific dangers.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.learningObjective: Interpret the appeal for refuge and its stated dangers, including its relation to An-Nās.
questions.prompt: A learner says that the speaker in Al-Falaq asks the night itself to provide protection. Correct the reading using verses 1 and 3.
questions.answer: Refuge is sought in Allah, addressed as Lord of daybreak. The night is mentioned in connection with danger.
questions.explanation: The object of the appeal and the danger have different roles.

markingGuide.description: Distinguishes the role of night in verse 3.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.learningObjective: Interpret the appeal for refuge and its stated dangers, including its relation to An-Nās.
questions.prompt: Which feature of Al-Falaq 113:5 adds a danger connected with a person’s attitude towards another?
questions.answer: Its reference to the harm of envy.
options: Its description of a route taken by travellers.
Its list of rules for dividing property.
Its reference to the harm of envy.
Its description of the clothing of a visitor.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.learningObjective: Interpret the appeal for refuge and its stated dangers, including its relation to An-Nās.
questions.prompt: What role does the reference to blowing on knots have in Al-Falaq?
questions.answer: It identifies a harmful practice from which refuge is requested.
questions.explanation: The verse forms part of the appeal for protection.
options: It identifies a harmful practice from which refuge is requested.
It instructs the speaker to perform the practice.
It names the one to whom the request is addressed.
It gives a method for choosing a community leader.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.learningObjective: Interpret the appeal for refuge and its stated dangers, including its relation to An-Nās.
questions.prompt: Compare the descriptions used for the one addressed in Al-Falaq 113:1 and An-Nās 114:1–3. State one shared function and one difference in emphasis.
questions.answer: Both establish whom the speaker turns to for refuge. Al-Falaq invokes Allah in relation to daybreak, while An-Nas names His lordship, sovereignty and divinity in relation to humankind.
questions.explanation: The comparison concerns the openings of both surahs.

markingGuide.description: Explains their shared role in the appeal.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.learningObjective: Interpret the appeal for refuge and its stated dangers, including its relation to An-Nās.
questions.prompt: Both Al-Falaq and An-Nās ask for refuge. Explain how the dangers they describe give the two appeals different emphases.
questions.answer: Al-Falaq names several dangers, including darkness, harmful knot-blowing and envy. An-Nas focuses on whispering into human hearts from jinn and humans.
questions.explanation: The common purpose is developed through different descriptions of harm.

markingGuide.description: Identifies the range of dangers in Al-Falaq.
Explains the focus on whispering in An-Nas.
Connects the difference to their common appeal for refuge.
